api_calls._baseline_note_entry: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD — this entry REPLACES the baseline's `GET /api/risk/account-health` entry for the same caller (`api.risk.getMarginHealth`), which was recorded with `resolved: false`. That is the point: the baseline recorded a call NO ROUTER DECLARED, i.e. a 404 on every mount, and `pages/RiskSettings.jsx` rendered nothing for `margin_ratio`, `free_margin` and `risk_score` as a result. `api/modules/risk.js:64-76` carries the correction in the source — the read is repointed at `GET /api/risk/margin-health`, which `routers/risk.py:395` declares and which answers exactly those three figures, and the caller-less sibling `getAccountHealth` was deleted rather than repointed. So the entry is now `resolved: true` against `backend_app.routers.risk.get_margin_health`. A broken call becoming a working one is the only kind of api_calls change this file should ever accept without a matching frontend requirement.

api_calls._baseline_note_raises: AUTHORISED RE-RECORD — `GET /api/risk/strategy-limits` gained one raise: 503 STRATEGY_LIMITS_FETCH_FAILED. `raises` was EMPTY because the handler could not fail: a `strategy_limits` read that threw was caught, logged at DEBUG, and the request answered 200 with whatever the in-memory map held — on a fresh process `{"limits": [], "count": 0}`. An empty list and an unreadable list are different facts and they render identically: `pages/RiskSettings.jsx` titles the panel "Strategy capital allocations (0)" and shows nothing, which reads as "no per-strategy limits are configured". A trader who believes that may size a position as though no cap applies while the cap sits in a table this endpoint could not reach, and `paper_trading_service` goes on enforcing it. The response contract is otherwise UNCHANGED — `limits`, `count` and `user_id` keep their names, types and meaning on the success path, so no client that reads them is affected; what changed is that the failure path is now reachable and named instead of being disguised as a successful empty read. `tests/test_exception_swallow_regression.py::TestGetStrategyLimitsExceptionSwallow` is the test, and it was FAILING against the old behaviour. NOT closed here, deliberately: `sb is None` (no token, or `create_request_supabase_async` refused) still falls through to the in-memory store, and `GET /api/risk/settings` has the same shape over a defaulted record — both are recorded in docs/pre-existing-test-failures.md, because closing them means redefining what a `None` from the module-shared `_sb` means for every handler in `routers/risk.py`.
